metadata.name: Notice Response
metadata.description: Comprehensive vertical for responding to government and IRS notices: tax notices, collection notices, audit letters, deficiency notices, and official correspondence requiring formal response.

overview.purpose: Enable taxpayers and individuals to respond professionally and effectively to formal government notices within statutory deadlines, protecting rights and minimizing penalties.
overview.targetUser: Individuals and small business owners receiving IRS notices, government correspondence, or formal tax/collection letters who need professional responses.
overview.commonProblem: Government notices are complex, formal, and require responses within strict deadlines. Missing deadlines or inadequate responses can result in automatic acceptance of proposed adjustments, levies, or collection actions. Recipients often don't understand notice implications or response requirements.

workflows.description: 30 distinct notice response workflows covering IRS tax notices, collection notices, formal examination letters, deficiency notices, and collection procedures.

commonPatterns: Extraction Pattern: All 30 workflows extract taxpayer identifying info (name, SSN, tax year), proposed adjustments or claims, IRS reasoning, response deadlines, and supporting evidence requirements.

Validation Pattern: Core validations across all workflows: (1) deadline compliance, (2) address all proposed adjustments/claims, (3) provide supporting evidence, (4) avoid admitting liability, (5) professional format and tone.

Response Pattern: All responses follow structured business letter format with header (addressing correct IRS center), introduction, item-by-item response to adjustments/claims, professional closure, and signature with enclosures list.

domainKnowledge.description: Notice Response vertical requires deep knowledge of IRS procedures, tax law, collection procedures, statutory deadlines, and formal business correspondence.
requirements: Comprehensive understanding of Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Sections 6211, 6213, 6603, 7122 and Treasury Regulations
Knowledge of IRS examination procedures and Collection Due Process (CDP) rights per IRC 6330
Understanding of tax substantiation requirements and what constitutes acceptable evidence
Knowledge of statutory deadlines: 30 days for CP2000, 90 days for CP90 (Tax Court petition), etc.
Proficiency in formal business correspondence and professional tax communication
Understanding of defensive strategy vs. settlement strategy in tax disputes
Knowledge of Appeals Division procedures and when appeals are available
Understanding of Tax Court jurisdiction and petition procedures for CP90 notices
Knowledge of Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) calculation for Offer in Compromise
Understanding of installment agreements, payment plans, and currently-not-collectible status
resources: IRS Publication 556 - Examination of Returns, Appeal Rights, and Claims for Refund
IRS Publication 595 - Tax Guide for Commercial Fishermen
U.S. Tax Court Rules of Practice and Procedure
Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (for federal court litigation)
State tax statutes and regulations (for state notice responses)
Appeals and Collections Process Training Materials (ACPTM)
Case law on substantiation requirements and burden of proof in tax disputes

implementation.notes: Notice Response is the highest-priority template. It encompasses the most common and highest-volume workflows in the MailMyPDF ecosystem. All 30 workflows use the notice-response template engine but with domain-specific variations. Successful implementation requires careful attention to statutory deadlines (30 days for CP2000, 90 days for CP90, etc.) and precise extraction of IRS positions and taxpayer identifying information.
commonChallenges: Extracting all proposed adjustments accurately when notices span multiple pages
Understanding the specific type of notice and appropriate response strategy (protest vs. appeal vs. payment arrangement)
Ensuring responses address ALL proposed adjustments - silence on even one item may be construed as agreement
Calculating statutory deadlines correctly and ensuring responses are submitted before deadline
Providing sufficient supporting evidence - assertions without documentation carry no weight
Avoiding common mistakes: admitting error, providing tax/legal advice, using aggressive tone, or missing required format elements
Coordinating responses when multiple notices are issued (e.g., CP2000 followed by CP90 after response period closes)
Understanding jurisdiction-specific variations for state tax notices
Managing complex cases with multiple adjustments, multiple tax years, or substantial amounts
